mu_name_from: MuMain loads MODEL_ARMOR + i from ArmorMale{i+1} (ZzzOpenData.cpp line 140), so file 06 is armour index 5, which openmu's 0.75 Armors.cs names the Leather Armor. mu.db agrees: code 4101, group 8 index 5, Player/ArmorMale06.bmd.
why_this_one: Martin's and Harold's +0 line, and the set the Armour select could offer only a glove of. The wandering merchants stock all five Leather pieces at +0 - the cheapest whole set in the game and the one a Dark Knight actually buys first - so four of their five lines were dropped by Realm.Shelf for want of a row. See shared/Market.Wandering.
profile_from: Not armour, whose default is plate_steel: nothing in this set is a forged plate. See profiles/soft_armour.json, which exists for these three sets.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Armors.cs. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: ArmorInitializerBase.CreateArmor(number, slot, width, height, name, dropLevel, defense, durability, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, darkWizardClassLevel, darkKnightClassLevel, elfClassLevel). `armor.Group = (byte)(slot + 5)`, so slot 2 is group 7, 3 is 8 and 4 is 9.
stats.defense_note: Points of defence, in the row and summed into Player.ArmourDefense by Wear - see shared/Rows.cs.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are 0, 1, 0 - the Dark Knight alone.

sheet_from: Data/Player/upper_07_m.OZJ (128x128), upper_07b_m.ozt (32x32), skin_barbarian_01.OZJ and hide_m.OZJ, from MuMain. The .bmd names upper_07_m.jpg, upper_07b_m.tga, skin_barbarian_01.jpg and hide_m.jpg; 106 of the 178 triangles are on the first, 16 on the tabard, 44 on the skin and 12 on hide.
sheet_note: upper_07_m is the cuirass front and back, a dark olive-black shell with pale highlights along every ridge and a raised boss at the sternum. Mean (120, 118, 111) at chroma 10. upper_07b_m is the tabard hanging from it: an olive strip with a white rune drawn down it, and its alpha cuts 4% - the strip's own edge. skin_barbarian_01 is the Dark Knight's own body sheet - face, neck and bare arms - which the piece carries because the armour does not cover them and MU draws the skin as part of the worn mesh. hide is MU capping the openings, a solid black square, as on ArmorMale10.
material_note: Four islands. Island 1 is 112 triangles and island 0 is 22 - together the cuirass, the tabard and hide's caps, 134 triangles welded into two shells - and both take leather. The tabard is inside island 1 rather than beside it, so the strip of cloth ships at hide's roughness; it is 16 triangles against 106 and the island is the unit, which is the same limit the Short Sword's pommel cap records. Islands 2 and 3 are 22 triangles each, 44 together, which is skin_barbarian_01's 44 exactly: the two bare arms. The face and the bare arms take skin, not the profile's leather, and the islands split them cleanly because MU draws them on a sheet of their own: each arm's mu_uv sits in the body sheet's limb column.
material_overrides_why: Leather at 0.75 rather than the library's 0.62, and the difference is how much of the model wears it. That 0.62 was settled on the bare Dark Knight's bracers - small trims among skin and cloth, where the note says a modest sheen is what separates oiled leather from bark, and it is right there. A whole suit of it is a different question: over a torso, a skirt and two legs the same sheen compounds into broad wet highlights down the thighs and across the skirt, and the set reads as vinyl. Swept in Blender under the rig from MU2/lighting.json at 0.62, 0.75 and 0.88 - at 0.62 the highlights are wet, at 0.88 the hide goes dead flat, and 0.75 keeps the sheen without the plastic. Scoped to this set rather than moved in the library, so the bracers keep the number that was measured for them.
